intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency-2 (COQ10D2) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the PDSS1 gene (607429) on chromosome 10p12.

paragraphs.text: Primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency-2 is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by a defect in the first steps of CoQ10 biosynthesis. Reported patients have had sensorineural hearing loss followed by optic atrophy, mild intellectual disability, muscle weakness, and cardiac valvulopathy. More severe early-onset multisystem forms, with encephalopathy, lactic acidosis, and death in early childhood, have also been described (Nardecchia et al., 2021; Bellusci et al., 2021).

paragraphs.text: Mollet et al. (2007) reported a family with an inborn error of CoQ10 biosynthesis and oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) deficiency. In their summary of previously published cases, Nardecchia et al. (2021) described the 2 sibs reported by Mollet et al. (2007), a 22-year-old male and a 14-year-old female. Both had neurosensorial deafness, optic atrophy, mild intellectual disability, muscular weakness, and cardiac involvement consisting of mild to moderate valvulopathy. They also had lactic acidosis, macrocephaly, peripheral neuropathy, and obesity/livedo reticularis. In these sibs the neurosensorial hearing loss came before the optic atrophy.

paragraphs.text: Nardecchia et al. (2021) reported 2 sisters born to consanguineous Egyptian parents. The proband was a 16-year-old girl. Her motor development was normal, and she walked independently at 15 months, but she had severe language delay. Profound bilateral sensorineural hearing loss was found at age 4 years. After she was fitted with a prosthesis she could speak simple sentences, but difficulty with verbal comprehension persisted, and mild intellectual disability was later diagnosed. She was referred at age 14 years for progressive visual loss. Her visual acuity had been normal at age 11 years and was 1/10 bilaterally at age 14 years. She had red-green dyschromatopsia, optic atrophy prevalent in the inferior temporal sector, visual evoked potentials with increased P100 latency and reduced amplitude, and bilateral reduction of retinal nerve fiber layer thickness on optical coherence tomography. Neurologic examination showed diffuse mild muscle weakness and mild postural tremor of the upper limbs, and brain MRI was normal. Echocardiography showed a moderately dysplastic mitral valve with moderate insufficiency, medium-grade tricuspid insufficiency with an estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure of 40 mm Hg, and a moderately dilated left atrium. Her 6-year-old sister had bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. At age 6 years she developed decreased visual acuity, and examination showed optic atrophy with bilateral temporal pallor of the optic nerve head, as well as divergent strabismus. In both sisters the sensorineural hearing loss came before the optic atrophy.

paragraphs.text: Bellusci et al. (2021) reported a boy born prematurely after an in vitro fertilization pregnancy complicated by twin-twin transfusion. At age 5 months he had failure to thrive, hypotonia, feeding difficulties, bilateral hearing impairment, pulmonary hypertension, livedo reticularis, and distal phalangeal erythema; the erythema persisted as a chronic sign. He went on to develop a progressive multisystem disorder with severe developmental delay, pyramidal dysfunction, seizures, tremor, optic atrophy and nystagmus, severe visual and hearing impairment, white matter cystic change, and chronic heart failure. He died at 3 years of age. Brain MRI showed mild cerebral atrophy at 12 months. At 24 months it showed cystic change in the white matter, with signal abnormalities and small necrotic or porencephalic cysts in the white matter tracts surrounding the lateral ventricles and in the commissural fibers; the U fibers, pyramidal tracts, and gray matter were spared.

paragraphs.text: In a family with CoQ10 deficiency and OXPHOS deficiency, Mollet et al. (2007) identified a homozygous mutation in the PDSS1 gene that results in an asp308-to-glu (D308E) substitution at a conserved residue. Yeast Deltacoq1 strains transformed with the corresponding mutant yeast COQ1 gene showed defective growth on respiratory medium. Nardecchia et al. (2021) gave the nucleotide change as c.924T-G and stated that the 2 affected sibs had deafness, optic atrophy, mild intellectual disability, muscle weakness, and valvulopathy.

paragraphs.text: In 2 sisters, born to consanguineous Egyptian parents, with sensorineural hearing loss followed by optic atrophy, Nardecchia et al. (2021) identified a homozygous c.735G-T transversion in the PDSS1 gene, resulting in a gln245-to-his (Q245H) substitution at a highly conserved residue. The variant was found by whole-exome sequencing and was not present in the gnomAD database. It lay within a 12-Mb region of homozygosity and segregated with the disorder in the family: both parents were heterozygous, and the unaffected sibs were heterozygous or homozygous wildtype.

paragraphs.text: Bellusci et al. (2021) reported a boy with primary CoQ10 deficiency who had mitochondrial encephalopathy, pulmonary hypertension, livedo reticularis, distal phalangeal erythema, and 3-methylglutaconic aciduria, and who died at age 3 years. In this patient they identified compound heterozygous mutations in the PDSS1 gene: a c.716T-G transversion, resulting in a val239-to-gly (V239G) substitution, and a c.1183C-T transition, resulting in an arg395-to-ter (R395X) substitution.
